Container.Name: openwakeword-trainer
Container.Overview: All-in-one openWakeWord trainer with a web UI. Type a wake word, record your own voice in the browser, then train a Home Assistant compatible .tflite and .onnx model. Kokoro TTS runs inside the container and generates thousands of blended voices, so nothing external is needed. Uses an NVIDIA GPU when one is passed through (install the Nvidia Driver plugin), otherwise everything runs on the CPU, just slower. Open the WebUI over HTTPS so the browser allows microphone recording. The first training run downloads about 19 GB of shared training data into the data folder.
Container.Requires: For GPU training install the Nvidia Driver plugin. No GPU? Remove --runtime=nvidia from Extra Parameters and it runs on the CPU.

Config.Name: HTTPS WebUI port
Config.Description: Web UI over HTTPS with a self-signed certificate. Browsers only allow the microphone over HTTPS, so use this one. Accept the certificate warning once.

Config.Name: HTTP WebUI port
Config.Description: Plain HTTP. Point a reverse proxy with a real certificate here. Microphone recording will not work over plain HTTP.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Wake word projects, your recordings, cached clips and about 19 GB of downloaded training data.

Config.Name: Model output
Config.Description: Finished .tflite and .onnx models are copied here after each training run.

Config.Name: Clips to review
Config.Description: Optional. Wake word clips from Home Assistant to sort on the Review clips tab, e.g. the wake-clip-keeper clips folder. Read only: nothing in it is changed.

Config.Name: Speech-to-text server
Config.Description: Optional, for the Review clips tab: a Wyoming speech-to-text server, the same one Home Assistant uses, e.g. tcp://192.168.1.10:10300. It hears what was said when the wake word fired.

Config.Name: Speech-to-text language
Config.Description: Language code sent to the speech-to-text server.

Config.Name: NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES
Config.Description: Which GPU to use: all, or a GPU UUID from the Nvidia Driver plugin page.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User ID that owns created files (99 = nobody).

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group ID that owns created files (100 = users).

Config.Name: Certificate hostnames
Config.Description: Optional comma separated IPs or hostnames to put in the self-signed certificate, e.g. 192.168.1.10,tower.local. Delete the certs folder in Data to regenerate.

Config.Name: Hugging Face token
Config.Description: Optional. Only needed if Hugging Face rate limits the training data download.
